name: scratch
title: Scratch
description: Create disposable scratch folders and clean up the ones you have stopped touching.
author: jakeobsen

commands.name: create-scratch
commands.title: Create Scratch
commands.description: Creates a randomly named folder under the scratch root and opens it in your editor.

commands.name: scratch-folders
commands.title: Scratch Folders
commands.description: Browse scratch folders, open them, and clean up the ones untouched for the configured number of days.

preferences.name: scratchRoot
preferences.title: Scratch Root
preferences.description: Directory that holds scratch folders. Leave blank to use ~/scratch.

preferences.name: editorApp
preferences.title: Editor
preferences.description: App the new scratch folder is opened in.

preferences.name: openInEditor
preferences.title: After Creating...
preferences.label: open in editor
preferences.description: Uncheck to only create the folder and copy its path to the clipboard.

preferences.name: staleDays
preferences.title: Stale After (Days)
preferences.description: A scratch folder counts as stale when nothing inside it has been modified for this many days.

preferences.name: nameStyle
preferences.title: Folder Name Style
preferences.description: Shape of the generated folder name.

preferences.name: terminalApp
preferences.title: Terminal App
preferences.description: Terminal opened by ⌘T, and used to host the git client (Terminal.app, kitty, and iTerm2 are supported).

preferences.name: gitClientApp
preferences.title: Git Client Command
preferences.description: Shell command run inside the terminal at the folder root by ⌘G (e.g. lazygit, gitui, tig).

preferences.name: deleteMode
preferences.title: Delete Mode
preferences.description: Trash is recoverable from Finder; permanent delete is not.
